own_solution.law: Stated tunnelling model T = exp(-2 kappa a), kappa = sqrt(2 m (V0 - E))/hbar; equal particle fluxes and equal charge (+e) give I_p/I_d = T_p/T_d = exp(2 a (kappa_d - kappa_p))
assumptions: prescribed transmission formula with no prefactor (stated)
equal particle rates (stated), both particles charge +e
V0 - E = 0.4 eV for both (same kinetic energy)

T2708.regime: Thermal energy spread negligible compared with the 0.4 eV barrier excess (0.028 eV << 0.4 eV), so the stated monoenergetic exponential model applies

TAEE0.regime: Thermal energy spread negligible compared with the 0.4 eV barrier excess (0.028 eV << 0.4 eV)

notes: U = 0.4 eV = 6.40871e-20 J; m_p = 1.672633e-27 kg; kappa_p = sqrt(2 m_p U)/hbar = 1.464201e-23/1.0546e-34 = 1.388395e11 m^-1; kappa_d = kappa_p sqrt(2.01355/1.00728) = 1.388395e11 x 1.413859 = 1.962995e11 m^-1; 2a(kappa_d - kappa_p) = 6e-11 x 5.74600e10 = 3.4476; ratio = e^3.4476 = 31.42. With 0.55 eV: exponent x sqrt(1.375) = 4.0427, ratio = 56.98. Incident current 5.2 nA per beam: same charge so equal currents is equivalent to equal particle rates; the current multiplies both transmitted currents and cancels (C). Thermal energy sentences: under the prescribed model they do not enter; I classify as K (would matter only if the energy spread were comparable to the 0.4 eV barrier excess); D would also be defensible. The 'step at the guard electrode' is a separate electrode beside the barrier, not the barrier the beams strike, so D. Pairs: TC752/TEED5 and T2708/TAEE0 are wording variants with identical numbers; TF273/T7B68/T87E1/TF88C all 0.15 eV; TE9A5/T1B32 are numeral-free ('a little').
